audit_findings.title: The share denominator may be understated by roughly 10 million shares
audit_findings.magnitude: 0-share shortfall against the filed July 24, 2026 count; the 235.700812 million valuation denominator is 2.214 million, or 0.95%, above the filed 233.486812 million basic shares
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 20, 2026, there were 243,141,405 outstanding shares of the registrant’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share.
audit_findings.explanation: The suspected transcription error is disproved by the supplied 10-Q: it expressly reports 233,486,812 shares, while 10.5 million shares were repurchased during the first half of 2026. The valuation then adds 2.214 million shares for dilution, so the denominator is not understated on the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Retain the 235.700812 million denominator and document its reconciliation as 233.486812 million filed basic shares plus 2.214 million dilutive shares.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI is an unbridged cash claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $242 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.03 per valuation share and 1.64% of the $14.747 billion base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: The holders of the non-controlling interest in Idrica, a consolidated subsidiary of the Company, have a right to sell the remaining equity interest in Idrica to the Company for cash (the “Put Right”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: consolidated cash is added without recognizing the filed Idrica claim ahead of common equity. Deducting $242 million would reduce base value from $62.57 to about $61.54 per share. That correction cannot close the $43.12 gap to the $105.69 market price or the $32.84 gap even to the $72.85 bull value, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario and the buy-below calculation with a separate $242 million redeemable-NCI deduction, or rebuild both OE and excess cash on a common-shareholder-only perimeter.

audit_findings.title: A noncash 2024 acquisition gain may contaminate the trend anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $152 million pre-tax, equal to 14.2% of reported 2024 OE; tax-adjusted anchor and valuation effects unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the remeasurement of its previously held equity interest, the Company recognized a gain of approximately $ 152 million in the fourth quarter of 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The noncash remeasurement gain is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE worksheet removed it. If retained, it inflates the 2024 observation used in the log-trend anchor; if already removed, there is no error. The tax-adjusted amount entering OE and its resulting trend effect cannot be established from the supplied valuation summary.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2024 OE reconciliation, remove the gain and its actual tax effect if present, refit the ten-year log trend, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Outsourced-water investment may be required reinvestment outside reported capital expenditures
audit_findings.magnitude: $146 million 2025 increase in long-term receivables, equal to 15.2% of the $958.8 million anchor; recurring or omitted portion unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: The $22 million year-over-year decrease was primarily driven by an increase spending on long-term outsourced water projects, the liquidation of customer advances and deferred revenue, increased payments for strategic investments, and higher restructuring payments.
audit_findings.explanation: The $146 million cash use is demonstrated and is large relative to normalized OE. What remains unresolved is whether the OE worksheets already captured it and how much represents recurring investment necessary to sustain outsourced-water revenue rather than temporary project timing. A recurring omitted component of this scale is reasonably capable of materially lowering OE and intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Trace long-term receivables and outsourced-project cash spending through each historical OE worksheet, classify maintenance or growth reinvestment versus temporary working capital, and rerun the anchor and scenarios using the supported recurring deduction.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal could disappear if its depreciation was added back
audit_findings.magnitude: $36 million 2025 finance-lease ROU depreciation, $33 million 2025 principal payments, and $125 million filed lease liabilities; $33 million equals 3.4% of the anchor
audit_findings.evidence: Our current finance lease liabilities of $ 34 million and $ 27 million are included in accrued and other current liabilities as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes the depreciation, principal payments, and liability, but the record does not show whether the OE worksheets added back the $36 million depreciation. If they did so without deducting principal or replacement economics, recurring OE is overstated. The possible annual mismatch is modest relative to the anchor, but treatment across the ten-year series is unknown, so materiality cannot be closed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile eligible D&A to finance-lease ROU depreciation for every historical year; if added back, deduct normalized principal or supported replacement spending, rerun the valuation, and separately disclose the $125 million lease liability in debt context.

audit_findings.title: One-time tax benefits may remain in the earnings history
audit_findings.magnitude: $42 million 2025 deferred-tax benefit, equal to 4.0% of 2025 OE and 4.4% of the anchor; earlier-year effect unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 effective tax rate differs from that of 2024 primarily due to the tax effects of the gain on remeasurement of equity interest in the prior period, partially offset by one-time deferred tax benefits from internal reorganizations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $42 million 2025 benefit is demonstrated, but its treatment in the OE history is not. Because the anchor is fitted across ten years and latest actual OE was not selected, this item alone does not translate dollar-for-dollar into the anchor. Earlier unusually low tax rates could increase the cumulative effect, but the supplied record does not quantify which portions were nonrecurring or already normalized.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile reported tax expense to normalized cash taxes for all ten years, remove identified discrete reorganization benefits and releases consistently, refit the trend, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $88 million in 2024, equal to 15.7% of filed D&A, 8.2% of 2024 OE, and 9.2% of the anchor; eligible portion unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2024 $88.0m (15.7% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement error is demonstrated because the unidentified residual was left as an expense. Any eligible non-economic component would make OE and value higher, but the record does not identify the residual components or establish how much qualifies for add-back. Its gross size warrants resolution even though the present treatment is conservative.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the filed fixed-asset, lease, software, and intangible-amortization detail supporting the $88 million residual; add back only components shown to be eligible, then refit the trend and rerun the scenarios.
